claims.text: Increasing aluminum concentration in a multiprincipal-element alloy promotes formation of a continuous Al2O3 surface scale during high-temperature oxidation.
The aluminum-promoted Al2O3 scale is adherent.
A continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale governs oxidation resistance by reducing oxygen ingress.
The Al2O3 scale helps preserve material integrity by mitigating oxidation-induced stresses.
Increased aluminum content facilitates rapid selective oxidation and formation of an Al2O3 layer during high-temperature exposure.
The resulting Al2O3 layer grows slowly after it forms.
The Al2O3 layer limits further oxidation.
The Al2O3 layer delays detrimental oxide-scale spallation.
Limiting oxidation and delaying scale spallation maintains mechanical integrity under harsh high-temperature conditions.
Relative to the lower-aluminum baseline, the aluminum-enhanced alloy will show lower oxidation-related mass gain under identical exposure conditions.
Relative to the baseline, the aluminum-enhanced alloy will form a more uniform and adherent oxide scale.
Relative to the baseline, the aluminum-enhanced alloy will retain mechanical properties better after high-temperature exposure.
The proposed behavior should hold across temperature and exposure-time regimes typical of harsh high-temperature service for alloys with similar processing histories.
